Parotid gland swelling also occurs during this disease caused by a para·myxo·virus. Along with measles and rubella, the MMR vaccine protects individuals from this disease.

In secondary Sjögren’s (“SHOW-grunz”) syndrome, salivary gland swelling often occurs alongside either lupus or this disease. Sufferers of this disease may possess elevated levels of anti-citrullinated protein antibodies in their blood.

bonuses.leadin: Only “Somewhere Over the Rainbow” tops Dooley Wilson’s performance of this song on AFI's “100 Years...100 Songs” list. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this jazz song that opens, “You must remember this, a kiss is still a kiss.” Ilsa Lund asks Sam to play this song in a scene set at Rick’s Cafe.

“As Time Goes By” plays during Allan and Linda’s first kiss in Play It Again, Sam, an early collaboration between Diane Keaton and this actor. The pair reunited in Annie Hall and Manhattan, both directed by this actor.

In a film by this director, Barbra Streisand’s character seduces a musicologist to a duet of “As Time Goes By.” At the end of another of this director’s films, a housewife played by Cloris Leachman berates and then consoles her teenage ex-lover.

bonuses.leadin: Fringe theorists have surmised that the circular rings of this feature were evidence of a lost civilization because the shape matches Plato’s description of Atlantis. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this geological dome near the town of Chinguetti. This feature’s concentric circles were actually formed by an igneous intrusion deforming other layers of rock and not Atlantean technology.

The Richat Structure is located in this country in the southwestern end of the Sahara. The Senegal River separates Senegal from this country, which also borders the disputed territory of Western Sahara.

The Richat Structure is part of this plateau in Mauritania, which separates its remote north from the more populated south of the country. The town of Atar and the ancient center of Chinguetti are in this plateau.

bonuses.leadin: In a poem about this feature, the speaker watches a melon-rind go by and states “I am he who has gazed a hundred thousand years / On that which he now sees for the first time.” For 10 points each:
parts: What feature is described as “beautiful” and “blue” in a Karl Isidor Beck poem that inspired a waltz by Johann Strauss II?

This Hungarian poet of “By the Danube” described his “native country” as the place where his tombstone will “not for once misspell my name.” This socialist summed up his life in a “Curriculum Vitae” before dying at age 32.
This earlier poet wrote a “hymn” about the Ister, or Danube, that a 1942 lecture course by Martin Heidegger reads against the choral odes of Sophocles.
